posts.trend: A Bengaluru landlord has allegedly refused to rent a flat to Shark Tank India Season 5 contestant Aaditya Aanand because he runs a startup instead of earning a regular salary.
posts.context: 30-year-olds who quit stable corporate jobs to start businesses discover that Indian housing still treats entrepreneurship as unemployment.
posts.angle: A Bengaluru landlord runs tougher due diligence on a founder than any venture investor ever did.

landing_options.line: Pitch deck rakho. Kal Form 16 leke aana.
Investor maan gaya. Aunty ka broker nahi maana.
40 logon ko salary dete ho. Pehle apni dikhao.
Company aapki hai, isliye flat nahi milega.

slides: Investor ne 10 minute mein haan bola. Landlord ne mana kar diya.

"40 logon ko salary deta hoon."
"Acha. Aapka Offer Letter?"
"Main founder hoon."
"Toh kisi senior se sign karwao."
Pitch deck rakho. Kal Form 16 leke aana.
posts.caption: That one friend who left a stable corporate job to build something and now cannot rent a 2BHK.

tweet.setup: Investor took 10 minutes to fund my startup. My Bengaluru landlord took 2 minutes to reject my tenant application.
tweet.punch: He asked for an offer letter signed by my manager.

messages.text: Sir owner ko aapka company profile samajh nahi aaya
Bhai TV pe aaya tha pichle mahine. Funding mili hai.
Owner bol rahe hain koi MNC ka payslip hai toh bhejo
Main hi boss hoon bhai, khud ko payslip kaise doon
Sir toh 2BHK mushkil hai, unko stable salary chahiye

posts.rank_verdict: Slide 2's dialogue with the broker is funnier than the landing, and putting Form 16 in the final line hurts global legibility.
